content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–10 days ahead) when prices are trending downward.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 70→75 range) — model overshoots and fails to correct downward momentum.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift toward historical averages too quickly, missing recent volatility.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <65) — model flattens out too early, ignoring potential rebounds.
- Overestimates volatility in high-price regimes (e.g., >75) — model overreacts to spikes, creating artificial “overhang” in forecasts.
- Lagged response to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward, often missing the immediate correction.
- Forecasts tend to be too conservative in the final 5–10 days — underestimates rebound potential after corrections.
- High correlation between forecast and true outcome in 1–3 day horizon, but diverges sharply beyond 7 days — model loses predictive power over longer horizons.
